sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Zolinkano-Youngs, filling in as hoSt.

sentences.en: Over the past decade, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在过去十年里，美国

sentences.en: military experienced a wake-up call.
sentences.zh: 军队经历了一次警钟。

sentences.en: Research showed that traumatic brain injuries were not just caused by bombings and explosions, but also by the shockwaves troops feel from their own weapons,
sentences.zh: 研究表明，创伤性脑损伤不仅是由爆炸和轰炸引起的，还由部队在操作自身武器时感受到的冲击波引起，

sentences.en: like artillery and shoulder-fired rockets.
sentences.zh: 比如火炮和肩扛式火箭弹。

sentences.en: Now, new reporting shows that similarly devastating impacts can come from another unexpected place.
sentences.zh: 现在，新的报道显示，类似的破坏性影响可能来自另一个意想不到的地方。

sentences.en: The ocean.
sentences.zh: 海洋。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Dave Phillips on a significant blind spot in the Coast Guard.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事Dave Phillips将讲述海岸警卫队中一个重大的盲点。

sentences.en: And the teenager who helped expose how widespread the danger really is.
sentences.zh: 以及那位帮助揭露危险程度究竟有多广泛的青少年。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, September 1St.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月1日，星期二。

sentences.en: Dave Phillips, you have been covering the military for how long?
sentences.zh: Dave Phillips，你报道军队有多久了？

sentences.en: Probably like 20 years.
sentences.zh: 大概20年了吧。

sentences.en: And I think it's fair to say that you have expanded our understanding of specifically brain injuries in the military and how they can impact a wide range of jobs.
sentences.zh: 我认为可以肯定地说，你扩展了我们对军队中脑损伤的专门理解，以及它们如何影响各种各样的工作。

sentences.en: But recently, your reporting took you to a branch of the military that I think most of us would not associate with head trauma.
sentences.zh: 但最近，你的报道把你带到了一个我认为我们大多数人不会将其与头部创伤联系起来的军种。

sentences.en: And that's the Coast Guard.
sentences.zh: 那就是海岸警卫队。

sentences.en: How'd you end up there?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么接触到那里的？

sentences.en: Yeah, basically it started in Iraq because brain injuries were a huge part of the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 嗯，基本上是从伊拉克开始的，因为脑损伤是伊拉克和阿富汗战争中一个巨大的组成部分。

sentences.en: IEDs going off, people getting really shaken up, but not having a scratch on them.
sentences.zh: 简易爆炸装置（IED）爆炸，人们被震得非常厉害，但身上却连一道划痕都没有。

sentences.en: And so we started to talk about these invisible injuries.
sentences.zh: 所以我们开始谈论这些隐形伤害。

sentences.en: And of course, I wrote about that years ago.
sentences.zh: 当然，我几年前就写过这个。

sentences.en: But it was only recently that I started to figure out that you could get those injuries not from some big blast that comes from the enemy,
sentences.zh: 但直到最近我才开始意识到，你可能并不是因为来自敌人的某种大爆炸而受到这些伤害，

sentences.en: but from multiple small blasts that come from firing your own weapon.
sentences.zh: 而是来自发射自己武器时产生的多次小爆炸。

sentences.en: So people that work on artillery cannons or mortars or fire shoulder-fired rockets.
sentences.zh: 所以那些操作火炮、迫击炮或发射肩扛式火箭弹的人。

sentences.en: These people are repeatedly getting a shock wave that whips through their brain tissue.
sentences.zh: 这些人反复受到冲击波的袭击，冲击波穿过他们的大脑组织。

sentences.en: And over time, those repeated shocks to the brain can lead to a really lasting and disruptive issue.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，这些对大脑的反复冲击会导致一个非常持久且具有破坏性的问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So you're describing heavy weapons, working with explosives.
sentences.zh: 所以你描述的是重型武器，使用爆炸物。

sentences.en: You're describing combat.
sentences.zh: 你描述的是战斗。

sentences.en: And I don't usually associate all of those things with the Coast Guard.
sentences.zh: 我通常不会把所有这些事情与海岸警卫队联系起来。

sentences.en: So I guess, were you surprised that your journey brought you here to the Coast Guard?
sentences.zh: 所以我猜，你的旅程把你带到海岸警卫队，你感到惊讶吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, because most people, when they think about the Coast Guard, they think like EMS for the sea.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为大多数人在想到海岸警卫队时，会想到海上的紧急医疗服务。

sentences.en: You know, like search and rescue, port safety, drug interdiction.
sentences.zh: 你知道，比如搜救、港口安全、禁毒。

sentences.en: And while they do have some weapons training, that's not what we really associate them with.
sentences.zh: 虽然他们确实有一些武器训练，但这并不是我们真正把他们联系起来的事情。

sentences.en: So honestly, the Coast Guard wasn't even on my radar for these types of injuries.
sentences.zh: 所以老实说，海岸警卫队甚至不在我关注这些类型伤害的雷达范围内。

sentences.en: Until I got a call from a reader who said,
sentences.zh: 直到我接到一位读者的电话，她说，

sentences.en: Hey, I think the same thing happened to my husband, and he recently died.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我觉得同样的事情发生在我丈夫身上，他最近去世了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: She described symptoms of a boat driver in the Coast Guard that were exactly like the symptoms that I was seeing in these other folks.
sentences.zh: 她描述的海岸警卫队船员的症状，和我在这其他人身上看到的症状完全一样。

sentences.en: So I said, Hey, if this is happening to your husband and to other people who are doing the same job, help me find those people who are being exposed and are maybe also suffering.
sentences.zh: 所以我说，嘿，如果这发生在你丈夫身上，也发生在做同样工作的其他人身上，帮我找到那些正在遭受暴露、可能也正在受苦的人。

sentences.en: And she knew a lot of them.
sentences.zh: 她认识很多人。

sentences.en: And she quickly connected me with a woman named Jenna Bonner.
sentences.zh: 她很快就把我介绍给了一位名叫Jenna Bonner的女士。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So tell me about Jenna.
sentences.zh: 那么跟我说说Jenna吧。

sentences.en: So you guys ready to start?
sentences.zh: 你们准备好开始了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Jenna Bonner's in her 40s.
sentences.zh: Jenna Bonner四十多岁。

sentences.en: She's got four kids and she moved to a beautiful little spot in the mountains of North Carolina a number of years ago with her husband, Brett Bonner.
sentences.zh: 她有四个孩子，几年前和丈夫Brett Bonner搬到了北卡罗来纳州山区一个美丽的小地方。

sentences.en: What was your first impression of him?
sentences.zh: 你对他的第一印象是什么？

sentences.en: He was very fit.
sentences.zh: 他非常健壮。

sentences.en: Uh-huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Like total life of the party.
sentences.zh: 就像派对的灵魂人物。

sentences.en: His friends used to call him Big Dumb Animal.
sentences.zh: 他的朋友们过去常叫他“大笨兽”。

sentences.en: He was like a golden retriever.
sentences.zh: 他就像一只金毛寻回犬。

sentences.en: Jenna, she had met this guy when she was in college.
sentences.zh: Jenna，她在大学时就认识了这个家伙。

sentences.en: And he was this young, big, muscly, you know, as she describes him, hot guy who was a friend of her brother's.
sentences.zh: 他是一个年轻、高大、肌肉发达的，正如她所描述的那样，是个她哥哥朋友的帅哥。

sentences.en: And he pretty instantly fell in love with her.
sentences.zh: 而且他几乎立刻就爱上了她。

sentences.en: In fact, after they only meet each other a couple of times.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在他们只见过几次面之后。

sentences.en: He told my parents, he's like, hold on, I gotta go walk my future wife out to her car.
sentences.zh: 他对我父母说，他就像是，等一下，我得去送我未来的妻子去她的车上。

sentences.en: Are you serious?
sentences.zh: 你是认真的吗？

sentences.en: In front of, I mean, that level of confidence?
sentences.zh: 当着……我的意思是，那种自信程度？

sentences.en: In front of the...
sentences.zh: 当着……的面

sentences.en: He starts introducing her to other people as his future wife.
sentences.zh: 他开始向其他人介绍她是他的未来妻子。

sentences.en: Okay, not wasting time here.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这可真是一点时间都不浪费。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: It's just fun.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: Like very fun.
sentences.zh: 非常有趣。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I joke that I married him because he made me laugh.
sentences.zh: 我开玩笑说我嫁给他是因为他让我发笑。

sentences.en: And they got married pretty quickly.
sentences.zh: 他们很快就结婚了。

sentences.en: He was in the Coast Guard.
sentences.zh: 他在海岸警卫队工作。

sentences.en: And he wanted to become one of their elite rescue boat drivers, which is called a surfman.
sentences.zh: 他想成为他们精英救援船驾驶员中的一员，也就是所谓的“冲浪人”。

sentences.en: Dave, this may just be me, but what's a surfman?
sentences.zh: Dave，这可能只是我个人的问题，但什么是“冲浪人”？

sentences.en: Can you just explain that a little bit more?
sentences.zh: 你能再多解释一下吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以，可以，可以。

sentences.en: When a boat is out in distress, in a storm, stuck in big waves, someone has to go out there and rescue them.
sentences.zh: 当一艘船在风暴中遇险，被困在巨浪中时，必须有人出去营救他们。

sentences.en: And that person who's driving that boat is the surfman.
sentences.zh: 而那个驾驶那艘船的人就是“冲浪人”。

sentences.en: And these boats are built to withstand anything.
sentences.zh: 这些船是为了承受任何情况而建造的。

sentences.en: They can get knocked over by a 25-foot wave and then right themselves like a rubber ducky.
sentences.zh: 它们可以被25英尺高的海浪掀翻，然后像橡皮鸭一样自动扶正。

sentences.en: And so you can imagine that driving one of those in stormy seas and surf that's higher than a building, that takes a great deal of skill.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象，在暴风雨的海面上和比建筑物还高的浪潮中驾驶其中一艘船，需要极高的技巧。

sentences.en: So when he's starting his career, they move to the West Coast because that's where all the really rough surf is along the Pacific.
sentences.zh: 所以当他开始职业生涯时，他们搬到了西海岸，因为太平洋沿岸所有的巨浪都在那里。

sentences.en: And so that's where all the surfmen train.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是所有“冲浪人”训练的地方。

sentences.en: And he's really excited.
sentences.zh: 他非常兴奋。

sentences.en: He gets stationed at the Coast Guard station that's right under the Golden Gate Bridge by San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 他被派驻到旧金山金门大桥下的海岸警卫队站。

sentences.en: And he and Jenna get established there.
sentences.zh: 他和Jenna在那里安了家。

sentences.en: He was just not the guy who was going to sit at a desk.
sentences.zh: 他根本不是那种会坐在办公桌前的人。

sentences.en: And he loved being on the boat.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢在船上。

sentences.en: He loved being underway.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢出海。

sentences.en: He was always the guy who was, like, helping people.
sentences.zh: 他总是那个乐于助人的人。

sentences.en: And he reaches his goal and he becomes a surfman.
sentences.zh: 他实现了目标，成为了一名“冲浪人”。

sentences.en: He joins this elite club.
sentences.zh: 他加入了这个精英俱乐部。

sentences.en: But when he gets there, he's doing these daily search and rescue missions.
sentences.zh: 但当他到达那里时，他每天都在执行搜救任务。

sentences.en: But a lot of it's not really rescue.
sentences.zh: 但其中很多并不是真正的营救。

sentences.en: It's recovering bodies from people who had jumped off the bridge.
sentences.zh: 而是从那些从桥上跳下的人身上打捞尸体。

sentences.en: Later, he said, I joined the Coast Guard to save lives.
sentences.zh: 后来，他说，我加入海岸警卫队是为了拯救生命。

sentences.en: Like, not this.
sentences.zh: 不是为了这个。

sentences.en: And that empathetic side of him really struggled with the jumpers.
sentences.zh: 他那富有同情心的一面在面对跳桥者时真的非常挣扎。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Just, like, what if I had, like, spotted them faster?
sentences.zh: 只是，如果我能更快地发现他们会怎样？

sentences.en: What if I, because he...
sentences.zh: 如果我……因为他……

sentences.en: And the job really started to weigh on him because he's a lifesaver.
sentences.zh: 这份工作真的开始让他感到沉重，因为他是一个救生员。

sentences.en: He got into this work to save people.
sentences.zh: 他从事这份工作是为了拯救人们。

sentences.en: And he had plenty who weren't all the way dead and were begging them to save them.
sentences.zh: 他遇到了很多还没完全断气、乞求他们救救自己的人。

sentences.en: And they weren't able to save them.
sentences.zh: 但他们却无法救活他们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And in a lot of these cases, these people couldn't be saved once they jumped to their deaths.
sentences.zh: 在很多情况下，这些人一旦跳下自杀就无法获救。

sentences.en: And even worse, there were people who were right on the edge.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，有些人就在边缘徘徊。

sentences.en: And his crew would have to perform all sorts of life-saving and CPR actions on them, even though it was pretty clear they weren't going to make it.
sentences.zh: 他的船员不得不对他们进行各种救生和心肺复苏操作，尽管很明显他们活不下来了。

sentences.en: Oh, my goodness.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: I'd imagine that that takes a toll.
sentences.zh: 我想这会造成很大的心理负担。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Jenna started to notice changes in him.
sentences.zh: Jenna开始注意到他的变化。

sentences.en: She noticed that he was having trouble sleeping, that his mood is really changing.
sentences.zh: 她注意到他睡眠困难，情绪也在发生巨大变化。

sentences.en: And it wasn't long before he was diagnosed by the Coast Guard with PTSD.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，他就被海岸警卫队诊断出患有创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）。

sentences.en: PTSD, post-traumatic stress disorder.
sentences.zh: PTSD，创伤后应激障碍。

sentences.en: And how does he respond to that?
sentences.zh: 他是怎么应对的？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, he takes it seriously.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，他很认真地对待。

sentences.en: He starts taking an antidepressant.
sentences.zh: 他开始服用抗抑郁药。

sentences.en: He goes to counseling.
sentences.zh: 他去接受心理咨询。

sentences.en: Ultimately, though, he goes back to work.
sentences.zh: 不过最终，他还是回到了工作岗位。

sentences.en: He's back on the boats.
sentences.zh: 他回到了船上。

sentences.en: And then he is reassigned up to Washington at the mouth of the Columbia River to the surf school, where he's actually teaching other surfmen how to do this kind of work.
sentences.zh: 然后他被重新分配到华盛顿哥伦比亚河口的冲浪学校，在那里他实际上是在教其他“冲浪人”如何做这种工作。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So that sounds maybe like a really positive change.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能是一个非常积极的改变。

sentences.en: He's now teaching, which I imagine would be easier on the mental.
sentences.zh: 他现在在教书，我想这在心理上会更容易一些。

sentences.en: It takes less of a toll, no?
sentences.zh: 负担会减轻，不是吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The stress of all these rescue calls, of having to hold bodies out of the ocean, that's gone.
sentences.zh: 所有这些救援电话的压力，不得不从海里捞出尸体的压力，都没有了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But the physical punishment of this new job is way worse.
sentences.zh: 但这份新工作的身体折磨要严重得多。

sentences.en: Because if you're just a regular surfman at a regular surf station, you're only out in big pounding waves once in a while.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你只是普通冲浪站的普通“冲浪人”，你只是偶尔才会出海面对巨大的海浪。

sentences.en: Pretty rarely.
sentences.zh: 相当罕见。

sentences.en: But if you're at the surf school, you're out there teaching other people all day, every day.
sentences.zh: 但如果你在冲浪学校，你每天都在外面教别人。

sentences.en: And you're not just in this big crashing surf.
sentences.zh: 而且你不仅仅是在巨大的破碎浪潮中。

sentences.en: You're in it with student drivers.
sentences.zh: 你是在和学员驾驶员一起。

sentences.en: And so if Brat's driving the boat, it's a much smoother ride.
sentences.zh: 所以如果Brett在驾驶船只，行驶会平稳得多。

sentences.en: You're on the boat.
sentences.zh: 你在船上。

sentences.en: He knows how to time it.
sentences.zh: 他知道如何把握时机。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He has the finesse.
sentences.zh: 他很有技巧。

sentences.en: He has years of experience.
sentences.zh: 他有多年经验。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he would say it's so much worse because, like, you're getting slammed around unnecessarily.
sentences.zh: 所以他会说情况要糟糕得多，因为你会被不必要地猛烈撞击。

sentences.en: And so what would have been a rough ride anyway becomes even rougher.
sentences.zh: 原本就很颠簸的航程变得更加颠簸了。

sentences.en: Right, okay, this is making sense.
sentences.zh: 对，好吧，这说得通。

sentences.en: I'm thinking about getting into a car with a 16-year-old who's trying to get their driver's permit.
sentences.zh: 我在想，如果坐进一辆由16岁正在考驾照的孩子开的车里。

sentences.en: But in that situation, I'm not in the ocean, and I don't have to deal with 12 to 15-foot dangerous waves coming at me.
sentences.zh: 但在那种情况下，我不在海里，也不用面对12到15英尺高的危险巨浪向我袭来。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Even when this type of training goes right, it's really, really rough.
sentences.zh: 即使这种训练进行得很顺利，过程也非常非常艰苦。

sentences.en: And when you're dealing with students and with stormy seas, oftentimes things go wrong.
sentences.zh: 当你面对学员和风暴海域时，事情往往会出错。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Honestly, I don't think they're looking for some larger cause, right?
sentences.zh: 老实说，我不认为他们在寻找什么更大的原因，对吧？

sentences.en: They're looking to just try and diagnose the patient that's in front of them.
sentences.zh: 他们只是想诊断眼前的病人。

sentences.en: So they say, hey, you probably have a brain injury here.
sentences.zh: 所以他们说，嘿，你这里可能患有脑损伤。

sentences.en: And maybe it's not surprising, considering this really active career of, you know, being out in giant waves.
sentences.zh: 考虑到他那充满活力的职业生涯，你知道，经常在巨浪中航行，这也许并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: Maybe you hit your head.
sentences.zh: 也许你撞到了头。

sentences.en: Maybe there was a boat accident.
sentences.zh: 也许发生过船只事故。

sentences.en: But even with the diagnosis, no one really tells him or his wife what to expect from a brain injury or how to handle it.
sentences.zh: 但即使有了诊断结果，也没有人真正告诉他和他的妻子，脑损伤会带来什么后果，或者该如何应对。

sentences.en: And everything that Brett is dealing with grows worse until it comes to a head on a winter morning in 2025.
sentences.zh: 布雷特所面临的一切都在恶化，直到2025年一个冬天的早晨，矛盾彻底爆发了。

sentences.en: Morning is fine.
sentences.zh: 早晨还好。

sentences.en: Church is great until I'm delayed at church.
sentences.zh: 教堂礼拜很棒，直到我在教堂耽搁了。

sentences.en: And then the grocery shop and he's just getting grumpier and grumpier.
sentences.zh: 然后去杂货店购物，他变得越来越暴躁。

sentences.en: And then the stuff by the door...
sentences.zh: 还有门口的那些东西……

sentences.en: It's a Sunday.
sentences.zh: 那是周日。

sentences.en: The family goes to church.
sentences.zh: 全家人去了教堂。

sentences.en: And after church, things get worse.
sentences.zh: 礼拜结束后，情况变得更糟了。

sentences.en: He's getting mad over little arguments that don't matter.
sentences.zh: 他因为一些无关紧要的小争执而发火。

sentences.en: And so all afternoon, things are sort of building.
sentences.zh: 所以整个下午，情绪都在不断积压。

sentences.en: And around dinner, he gets mad at his kids for leaving the house a mess.
sentences.zh: 晚餐时分，他因为孩子们把家里弄得一团糟而对他们发火。

sentences.en: And his response to that is he's going to take these boxes of Coast Guard files.
sentences.zh: 他的反应是，他要把这些装有海岸警卫队文件的箱子拿走。

sentences.en: And he's like, this needs to go.
sentences.zh: 他说，这些东西必须处理掉。

sentences.en: And I was like, no, I want it.
sentences.zh: 我说，不，我要留着它们。

sentences.en: And it goes in the boys' room.
sentences.zh: 于是它们被放进了男孩们的房间。

sentences.en: And just set it on fire in the living room fireplace.
sentences.zh: 然后他就在客厅的壁炉里把它们点着了。

sentences.en: Jen is looking at this from the kitchen, seeing her husband just, you know, ranting and angry.
sentences.zh: 珍（Jen）在厨房看着这一切，看到她的丈夫，你知道，在咆哮和愤怒。

sentences.en: And this fire and black smoke.
sentences.zh: 还有那火光和黑烟。

sentences.en: And it's just like, I don't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 我当时心想，我不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: She feels helpless.
sentences.zh: 她感到无助。

sentences.en: I literally actually think he might burn the house down.
sentences.zh: 我真的觉得他可能会把房子烧了。

sentences.en: So I should just take them.
sentences.zh: 所以我应该把它们带走。

sentences.en: We should just go.
sentences.zh: 我们应该离开这里。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: The only thing she can do, she feels, is get the kids out of the house.
sentences.zh: 她觉得她唯一能做的就是带孩子们离开家。

sentences.en: He's bent over in front of the fire.
sentences.zh: 他正弯腰站在火堆前。

sentences.en: And I was like, I'm going to go get dinner.
sentences.zh: 我说，我要去买晚餐了。

sentences.en: We'll be back.
sentences.zh: 我们一会儿回来。

sentences.en: I might have said, like, please don't burn the house down or something.
sentences.zh: 我可能说了句，请别把房子烧了之类的。

sentences.en: Like, juSt...
sentences.zh: 就像，只是……

sentences.en: I kind of was just like...
sentences.zh: 我当时只是觉得……

sentences.en: She packs up her four kids and she drives them to the nearest town where they go to Sonic.
sentences.zh: 她带上四个孩子，开车去了最近的城镇，去了索尼克（Sonic）快餐店。

sentences.en: Like, get them some dinner.
sentences.zh: 给他们买点晚餐。

sentences.en: And maybe by the time they get back, things will cool off.
sentences.zh: 也许等他们回来的时候，情况会冷静下来。

sentences.en: Well, while they're there, Brett calls the family on FaceTime.
sentences.zh: 好吧，当他们在那里时，布雷特通过FaceTime给家里打了电话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So I answer and he's like, don't bring the kids back tonight.
sentences.zh: 我接了电话，他说，今晚别带孩子们回来。

sentences.en: Don't bring the kids home tonight.
sentences.zh: 今晚别带孩子们回家。

sentences.en: And I was like, what?
sentences.zh: 我说，什么？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: We're juSt...
sentences.zh: 我们只是……

sentences.en: We're getting food and then we're coming home.
sentences.zh: 我们吃完饭就会回家。

sentences.en: Like, what is going on?
sentences.zh: 到底怎么了？

sentences.en: And he hangs up.
sentences.zh: 然后他挂断了电话。

sentences.en: And he says, don't bring the kids home.
sentences.zh: 他说，别带孩子们回家。

sentences.en: And he just hangs up.
sentences.zh: 然后他就挂了。

sentences.en: So they call him back.
sentences.zh: 于是他们又打回去。

sentences.en: And I see his face.
sentences.zh: 我看到了他的脸。

sentences.en: It's like, just dark.
sentences.zh: 看起来，一片阴暗。

sentences.en: It's dark.
sentences.zh: 很阴暗。

sentences.en: It's being lit by the screen.
sentences.zh: 只有屏幕的光照着他。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I only see his face.
sentences.zh: 我只看到了他的脸。

sentences.en: And he's got this really strange, vacant look.
sentences.zh: 他有一种非常奇怪、空洞的表情。

sentences.en: And he keeps telling them to turn their camera off on FaceTime.
sentences.zh: 他一直让他们在FaceTime上关掉摄像头。

sentences.en: And they're confused because they have turned their camera off.
sentences.zh: 他们很困惑，因为他们已经关掉了摄像头。

sentences.en: But they can still see him.
sentences.zh: 但他们仍然能看到他。

sentences.en: I'm like, hey, what's going on?
sentences.zh: 我说，嘿，怎么了？

sentences.en: Like, what's happening?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么事？

sentences.en: What's going on, Brett?
sentences.zh: 布雷特，怎么了？

sentences.en: And I'm like, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 我说，你是什么意思？

sentences.en: I'm coming back.
sentences.zh: 我正要回去。

sentences.en: Like, again, I'm trying to, like, talk rationally.
sentences.zh: 同样，我试图理性地沟通。

sentences.en: But I'm kind of frantic inside because I'm like, what is happening?
sentences.zh: 但我内心很慌乱，因为我在想，到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: They're all sitting in the car watching this as he keeps telling them to turn the camera off.
sentences.zh: 他们都坐在车里看着这一幕，而他一直让他们关掉摄像头。

sentences.en: And then suddenly the head of a pistol comes into the frame.
sentences.zh: 突然，一把手枪出现在镜头里。

sentences.en: Literally in a split second, you see the gun and he pulls the trigger.
sentences.zh: 就在那一瞬间，你看到了枪，然后他扣动了扳机。

sentences.en: And we all hear it.
sentences.zh: 我们都听到了。

sentences.en: There's a pop and a flash.
sentences.zh: 一声枪响，一道闪光。

sentences.en: And then the screen goes dark as the laptop that he's holding just tumbles into the darkness.
sentences.zh: 然后屏幕变黑了，因为他拿着的笔记本电脑掉进了黑暗中。

sentences.en: The whole family's just watched this happen.
sentences.zh: 全家人就这样目睹了这一切。

sentences.en: And there's this silence.
sentences.zh: 陷入了一片死寂。

sentences.en: Just everybody's there is stunned.
sentences.zh: 每个人都惊呆了。

sentences.en: And one of the kids says, did dad just drop the laptop?
sentences.zh: 其中一个孩子说，爸爸刚才是不是把笔记本电脑掉了？

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。

sentences.en: And Jenna has this moment where she's put together what happened.
sentences.zh: 珍在那一刻意识到发生了什么。

sentences.en: And she says, no, I think daddy shot himself.
sentences.zh: 她说，不，我想爸爸开枪自杀了。

sentences.en: That's awful.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: Suddenly he's gone with no note, with no explanation.
sentences.zh: 他突然离去，没有留下遗言，也没有任何解释。

sentences.en: And it really sent the whole family into this questioning.
sentences.zh: 这让整个家庭陷入了深深的质疑。

sentences.en: What the hell happened here?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是Wynna Liu。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的《Connections》谜题。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky.
sentences.zh: 我是Sam Mazursky。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天负责创作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”（promesthesia）的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的人们制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问nytimes.com/games，今天就开始玩吧。

sentences.en: Dave, so what does Brett Bonner's family do with this question of what happened to him?
sentences.zh: 戴夫，那么布雷特·邦纳的家人是如何看待他身上发生的事情这个问题的呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, man, suicide is so tough.
sentences.zh: 是啊，伙计，自杀真的太沉重了。

sentences.en: And it raises so many questions.
sentences.zh: 而且它引发了太多的疑问。

sentences.en: There's questions of blame.
sentences.zh: 有关于责备的疑问。

sentences.en: There's questions of what did we miss?
sentences.zh: 有关于我们错过了什么的疑问。

sentences.en: What could we have done?
sentences.zh: 我们本可以做些什么？

sentences.en: There's so many questions about what do you say about this legacy of this man who worked as a lifesaver for more than 20 years?
sentences.zh: 关于如何评价这位担任了20多年救生员的人的遗产，有太多的疑问了。

sentences.en: The family was so uncertain that when they buried him, they buried him with nothing on his headstone because they weren't sure what to say about him yet.
sentences.zh: 家人们当时非常迷茫，以至于在安葬他时，墓碑上什么都没写，因为他们还不确定该如何评价他。

sentences.en: So Brett's oldest daughter, Kaylee, she was going into her senior year of high school and she started thinking about this.
sentences.zh: 所以布雷特的大女儿凯莉，当时正要升入高三，她开始思考这个问题。

sentences.en: What were the questions you had when your dad died?
sentences.zh: 你父亲去世时，你有哪些疑问？

sentences.en: Like, I know it's like super complex, but in the months afterwards, what were the things you were kept turning over in your mind?
sentences.zh: 我知道这非常复杂，但在那之后的几个月里，你脑海中一直萦绕着什么问题？

sentences.en: Um, kind of just how it escalated so quickly.
sentences.zh: 嗯，大概就是事情怎么会升级得这么快。

sentences.en: Um, and how one thing kind of led to another because, I mean, I kind of got a front row seat to all of it because I was born right before he made surf.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有事情是怎么一件接一件发生的，因为，我是说，我几乎是全程见证了这一切，因为我是在他开始从事冲浪救援工作前不久出生的。

sentences.en: There were a lot of what ifs in her mind and one of them was sort of like this.
sentences.zh: 她脑子里有很多“如果……会怎样”的假设，其中一个大概是这样的。

sentences.en: What if all those years in the boats left him with some other brain injury?
sentences.zh: 如果那些年在船上的岁月给他留下了某种脑损伤呢？

sentences.en: And she started to look around on the web for information about that and she didn't find any.
sentences.zh: 她开始在网上搜索相关信息，但什么也没找到。

sentences.en: Definitely not from the Coast Guard.
sentences.zh: 海岸警卫队那边肯定是没有。

sentences.en: And so she said, okay, if I can't find any information from official sources,
sentences.zh: 所以她说，好吧，如果我从官方渠道找不到任何信息，

sentences.en: I'll have to go out and gather it myself.
sentences.zh: 那我就得自己去收集。

sentences.en: And she turned to the one source that she thought might actually have these answers.
sentences.zh: 于是她求助于她认为可能真正有答案的唯一来源。

sentences.en: And that was other people who did the same surfman job as her dad.
sentences.zh: 那就是其他和她父亲做同样冲浪救援工作的人。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So she has encountered this void of research into this and she's going to fill it.
sentences.zh: 所以她发现了这方面的研究空白，并打算填补它。

sentences.en: Tell us how she does that.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们她是怎么做的。

sentences.en: So her senior year, she's actually taking like a research class and she decides that her research project is going to be what happened to her dad.
sentences.zh: 在高三那年，她实际上选修了一门研究课程，并决定把她父亲身上发生的事作为研究课题。

sentences.en: And so she comes up with this questionnaire of about three dozen questions all about their brain health.
sentences.zh: 于是她设计了一份包含大约三打问题的问卷，全部关于他们的大脑健康。

sentences.en: And sends it out.
sentences.zh: 然后把它发了出去。

sentences.en: So I try to like make it short because I know that their attention span is really short because my dad's was.
sentences.zh: 我尽量让问卷简短，因为我知道他们的注意力持续时间很短，我父亲就是这样。

sentences.en: And to be clear, this is an academically rigorous process.
sentences.zh: 需要说明的是，这是一个学术严谨的过程。

sentences.en: It's an advanced placement class.
sentences.zh: 这是一门大学预修课程。

sentences.en: So her methods and questions, they have to be vetted and approved before she sends them out to these guys.
sentences.zh: 所以她的方法和问题在发给这些人之前，必须经过审核和批准。

sentences.en: How many people did you get to survey?
sentences.zh: 你调查了多少人？

sentences.en: Only 77.
sentences.zh: 只有77个。

sentences.en: That's a lot.
sentences.zh: 那已经很多了。

sentences.en: Well, I was hoping more, but.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我本来希望能有更多，但是……

sentences.en: This is a small population and they're hard to find.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很小的群体，而且很难找到他们。

sentences.en: Yeah, I was like individually.
sentences.zh: 是的，我当时是一个个去联系的。

sentences.en: And she gets 77 responses, both retired and active duty surfman, which is a pretty astounding number because this is a small and very insular group of people.
sentences.zh: 她收到了77份回复，来自退役和现役的冲浪救援队员，这是一个相当惊人的数字，因为这是一个很小且非常封闭的群体。

sentences.en: It's way more responses than I would have gotten as, you know, just a reporter showing up trying to talk to these people.
sentences.zh: 这比我作为一个记者跑去试图采访这些人所能得到的回复要多得多。

sentences.en: And I was just so amazed because here's this person who, because what she'd been through was almost like a reporting partner for me.
sentences.zh: 我感到非常惊讶，因为这个人，由于她所经历的一切，几乎成了我的报道伙伴。

sentences.en: And one big reason that she got this many responses and that's that her dad's Brett Bonner, a lot of these people had worked with him and knew him,
sentences.zh: 她能得到这么多回复的一个重要原因是，她父亲是布雷特·邦纳，这些人中有很多曾与他共事并认识他，

sentences.en: or at least they knew the story of what happened to him.
sentences.zh: 或者至少他们知道发生在他身上的故事。

sentences.en: And they really felt a duty to help his family out in any way they could.
sentences.zh: 他们真的觉得有义务尽其所能帮助他的家人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So she's covering ground that's completely new.
sentences.zh: 所以她正在探索一个全新的领域。

sentences.en: And she has no idea what she's going to find.
sentences.zh: 而且她完全不知道自己会发现什么。

sentences.en: And I looked at symptoms of TBI and I put that in there because I knew a lot of them wouldn't have diagnosed TBI.
sentences.zh: 我研究了创伤性脑损伤（TBI）的症状，并把它放了进去，因为我知道他们很多人可能并没有被诊断出TBI。

sentences.en: So it's like we can connect that maybe they have a possible TBI and we can.
sentences.zh: 所以我们或许能联系起来，他们可能患有潜在的TBI，我们可以做到。

sentences.en: And her driving question is, how many surfmen have traumatic brain injury or symptoms that look like a brain injury?
sentences.zh: 她的核心问题是，有多少冲浪救援队员患有创伤性脑损伤或看起来像脑损伤的症状？

sentences.en: And how is that impacting their lives?
sentences.zh: 这又是如何影响他们的生活的？

sentences.en: So, like, people said they had head injuries, but, like, I think a lot of them dismiss injuries that normal people would be like, oh, that's an injury.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们说他们受过头部损伤，但我认为他们很多人忽视了那些普通人会觉得“哦，那是受伤”的伤情。

sentences.en: And they'd be like, oh, that was just a scratch or something like that.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，哦，那只是擦伤之类的。

sentences.en: It sounds like from talking to you guys that if we'd asked your dad, have you ever had a head injury, he might have said no.
sentences.zh: 听你们这么说，如果我们问你父亲，你受过头部损伤吗，他可能会说没有。

sentences.en: He would have said only in peewee football.
sentences.zh: 他只会说在少年橄榄球赛时受过伤。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And when the questionnaires start coming back in, the answers are pretty astounding.
sentences.zh: 当问卷开始收回时，答案非常惊人。

sentences.en: She finds an overwhelming majority of these career surfmen who spent years and years in rough seas,
sentences.zh: 她发现绝大多数在波涛汹涌的大海中工作多年的职业冲浪救援队员，

sentences.en: very few of them had ever been diagnosed by the Coast Guard with a head injury.
sentences.zh: 很少有人被海岸警卫队诊断出头部受伤。

sentences.en: Very few of them believed they had a head injury, but almost all of them had the symptoms of a brain injury.
sentences.zh: 很少有人认为自己受过头部损伤，但几乎所有人都表现出了脑损伤的症状。

sentences.en: They were having the memory problems, the cognitive problems, the sleep problems, the mood problems,
sentences.zh: 他们有记忆问题、认知问题、睡眠问题、情绪问题，

sentences.en: all of the things that she was seeing in her dad, these guys were reporting to her.
sentences.zh: 她在她父亲身上看到的所有问题，这些人都在向她反馈。

sentences.en: And at the very end of her survey, she just left a blank spot where people could make any comment that they wanted.
sentences.zh: 在问卷的最后，她留了一个空白处，让人们可以写下任何他们想说的评论。

sentences.en: And I just want to read you a couple.
sentences.zh: 我想给你们读几条。

sentences.en: This one from a career surfman in his mid-50s.
sentences.zh: 这一条来自一位50多岁的职业冲浪救援队员。

sentences.en: He said,
sentences.zh: 他说，

sentences.en: My brain has started to fail me.
sentences.zh: 我的大脑开始衰退了。

sentences.en: I feel it.
sentences.zh: 我感觉到了。

sentences.en: I see it.
sentences.zh: 我看到了。

sentences.en: It's difficult to do things that used to come natural to me.
sentences.zh: 做那些曾经对我来说很自然的事情变得很困难。

sentences.en: And then another guy in his mid-40s.
sentences.zh: 还有另一位40多岁的人。

sentences.en: And remember, these are people who were the highest performing rescuers.
sentences.zh: 记住，这些人都是表现最出色的救援人员。

sentences.en: He wrote,
sentences.zh: 他写道，

sentences.en: It's been a struggle for me to keep my life together.
sentences.zh: 维持正常生活对我来说一直是一种挣扎。

sentences.en: The service members are describing in basically no uncertain terms, brain trauma.
sentences.zh: 这些服役人员基本上明确无误地描述了脑外伤。

sentences.en: But no one had asked them about it.
sentences.zh: 但没有人问过他们。

sentences.en: No one knew to ask them.
sentences.zh: 没有人知道该去问他们。

sentences.en: Yeah, but it's hard because it also looks like a lot of other things.
sentences.zh: 是的，但这很难，因为它看起来也像很多其他问题。

sentences.en: You know, if you're depressed and have nightmares and can't sleep and you've had a high-stress job for years,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你抑郁、做噩梦、睡不着觉，而且多年来一直从事高压工作，

sentences.en: it's very easy for people to say it's something else than brain injury.
sentences.zh: 人们很容易说这是脑损伤以外的其他原因。

sentences.en: And I think over and over again, even with the guys themselves, that's what they did.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，即使是他们自己，也一次又一次地这样认为。

sentences.en: No one ever questioned that this might be a physical injury from just doing the job.
sentences.zh: 从来没有人质疑过这可能是因为工作本身造成的身体伤害。

sentences.en: So basically through Kaylee's research and your subsequent reporting,
sentences.zh: 所以基本上通过凯莉的研究和你随后的报道，

sentences.en: you guys have found that the brain injuries that we associate with the stories that you were previously reporting on, right?
sentences.zh: 你们发现我们之前报道中提到的那些与故事相关的脑损伤，对吧？

sentences.en: The weapons, the other parts of the military, that that's also impacting the Coast Guard.
sentences.zh: 那些武器、军队的其他部门，这些也在影响着海岸警卫队。

sentences.en: It may even be widespread.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能已经很普遍了。

sentences.en: But I guess, Dave, I'm still curious how exactly folks like Brett were sustaining such severe brain trauma.
sentences.zh: 但我猜，戴夫，我仍然很好奇像布雷特这样的人究竟是如何遭受如此严重的脑外伤的。

sentences.en: These huge waves are hitting these boats.
sentences.zh: 巨大的海浪拍打着这些船只。

sentences.en: But walk me through how exactly that results in the brain injuries we've been describing.
sentences.zh: 但请带我了解一下这究竟是如何导致我们所描述的脑损伤的。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's what I wanted to figure out, too, because, like, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 是的，这也是我想弄清楚的，因为，我不知道。

sentences.en: I've been in boats on rough seas.
sentences.zh: 我曾在波涛汹涌的大海上坐过船。

sentences.en: I've been in big waves and I've gotten knocked around for sure.
sentences.zh: 我经历过大浪，肯定也被撞得东倒西歪过。

sentences.en: But it didn't seem like something that intense.
sentences.zh: 但看起来并没有那么剧烈。

sentences.en: And so I went back and saw if there was any other research on these boats and the kinds of forces that they deliver.
sentences.zh: 所以我回去查了一下，看看是否有关于这些船只及其产生的冲击力的其他研究。

sentences.en: And it turned out that there is.
sentences.zh: 结果发现确实有。

sentences.en: For a number of years, researchers in Europe have been looking at this problem
sentences.zh: 多年来，欧洲的研究人员一直在研究这个问题，

sentences.en: because crews on these types of boats get a lot of injuries to their knees, to their necks, to their backs,
sentences.zh: 因为这类船只的船员经常膝盖、脖子和背部受伤，

sentences.en: just from the rough ride, the repeated going up into the wave and slamming down into the backside.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是因为颠簸的航行，反复冲上浪尖又重重摔回浪底。

sentences.en: And even though they weren't looking for, you know, problems with brain injury, they found something really surprising that would explain this.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们当时并没有寻找脑损伤方面的问题，但他们发现了一些非常令人惊讶的事情，可以解释这一点。

sentences.en: And that is, in a nutshell, that a body standing on a boat acts a lot like a whip that gets cracked.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，站在船上的身体就像一条被甩动的鞭子。

sentences.en: The force at one end, where the feet are planted on the deck, is not that much.
sentences.zh: 在船尾，也就是双脚站立的地方，受到的力并不大。

sentences.en: But as that wave ripples up through the legs, through the back, and finally quickly jerks the neck, the force is many times what it was.
sentences.zh: 但当海浪穿过双腿、背部，最后迅速猛拉脖子时，力量是原来的许多倍。

sentences.en: So you might go through a wave that's hitting at only maybe six times the force of gravity.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能经历的海浪冲击力只有重力的六倍左右。

sentences.en: But by the time the neck jerks in the impact, when you slam into the trough, it could be the force of a car crash.
sentences.zh: 但当你在跌入浪谷时脖子猛地一震，那冲击力可能相当于一场车祸。

sentences.en: And so something that from the outside seems tame, the physics of it, at like a neuron level, is extremely violent.
sentences.zh: 所以从外表看似乎温和的事情，在神经层面的物理学上，却是极其剧烈的。

sentences.en: And if you apply that whip crack for a career, you know, let's say 10,000 wave hits, you start to understand how profoundly damaging this could be.
sentences.zh: 如果你在职业生涯中一直承受这种“鞭打”，比如1万次海浪冲击，你就会明白这可能有多大的破坏力。

sentences.en: So what can the Coast Guard actually do about it?
sentences.zh: 那么海岸警卫队实际上能对此做些什么呢？

sentences.en: What would prevention here actually look like?
sentences.zh: 这里的预防措施实际上会是什么样子？

sentences.en: I tell you, one of the most surprising things that happened in all of this reporting
sentences.zh: 我告诉你，在所有这些报道中最令人惊讶的事情之一，

sentences.en: was that when I picked up the phone and called the Coast Guard and warned them that I was going to do this story,
sentences.zh: 就是当我拿起电话打给海岸警卫队，警告他们我要做这个报道时，

sentences.en: that I was going to say, hey, your elite surfman rescue crews are getting brain injuries just from doing their job.
sentences.zh: 我要说，嘿，你们的精英冲浪救援队仅仅因为工作就受到了脑损伤。

sentences.en: The response I got from the person who picked up the phone was, good.
sentences.zh: 接电话的人给我的回应是，太好了。

sentences.en: I'm glad you're doing these stories.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你在做这些报道。

sentences.en: I was on boats like that for years.
sentences.zh: 我在那样的船上待了好几年。

sentences.en: And man, we always wondered about this.
sentences.zh: 伙计，我们一直对这个问题感到疑惑。

sentences.en: We never had any answers.
sentences.zh: 我们从来没有任何答案。

sentences.en: So there is a hunger to understand and solve this problem, which is the best place you can start, right?
sentences.zh: 所以人们渴望理解并解决这个问题，这是最好的起点，对吧？

sentences.en: Because there's a lot of things that potentially you could do.
sentences.zh: 因为有很多事情你可能可以做。

sentences.en: You could change the design of boats.
sentences.zh: 你可以改变船只的设计。

sentences.en: You could change the design of training.
sentences.zh: 你可以改变训练的设计。

sentences.en: You could change the shape of a career so that you never put one person in this rough surf for 20 years.
sentences.zh: 你可以改变职业生涯的规划，这样你就不会让一个人在汹涌的浪涛中工作20年。

sentences.en: There's lots of options, but it all starts from the same place.
sentences.zh: 有很多选择，但一切都从同一个地方开始。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it's worth noting this is not the way the government usually responds to an investigation.
sentences.zh: 是的，值得注意的是，这并不是政府通常对调查做出反应的方式。

sentences.en: It's obviously great to hear that the Coast Guard is responding to your reporting positively.
sentences.zh: 听到海岸警卫队对你的报道做出积极回应，显然很棒。

sentences.en: But I do wonder if there's reason to think that they are actually going to follow through with action here.
sentences.zh: 但我确实想知道，是否有理由认为他们真的会在这里采取行动。

sentences.en: Isn't there a world where they shouldn't have been relying on a motivated teenager in the first place to basically do their work for them?
sentences.zh: 难道不应该是一个他们本不该依赖一个有动力的青少年来替他们完成本职工作的世界吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's really frustrating, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的，这真的很令人沮丧，不是吗？

sentences.en: And I got to tell you, it's not unique to the Coast Guard.
sentences.zh: 我得告诉你，这在海岸警卫队并不是个例。

sentences.en: Listen, the Department of Defense has spent, and I'm not exaggerating here, billions of dollars on brain injury, studying it, understanding it, preventing it.
sentences.zh: 听着，国防部已经花费了——我在这里没有夸张——数十亿美元用于研究、理解和预防脑损伤。

sentences.en: And in every single case across every branch, they missed this kind of injury, the injury that comes from repeatedly doing a job that everyone has said is safe.
sentences.zh: 但在每一个分支机构的每一个案例中，他们都忽略了这种伤害，即反复从事每个人都说是安全的工作所带来的伤害。

sentences.en: So, yeah, it's a problem that they miss, even when they're trying to find it.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这是一个他们即使在努力寻找时也会忽略的问题。

sentences.en: It's a problem that they've ignored because it means fundamentally changing how you do things.
sentences.zh: 这是一个他们一直忽视的问题，因为它意味着从根本上改变做事方式。

sentences.en: But it's something that is now out in the open.
sentences.zh: 但现在这已经公开了。

sentences.en: And if it's out in the open because a teenager pointed it out, then good for her.
sentences.zh: 如果是因为一个青少年指出了这一点而公开，那对她来说是件好事。

sentences.en: Dave, I want to just take a step back here.
sentences.zh: 戴夫，我想退一步来看。

sentences.en: You've been covering brain injuries in the military for so long.
sentences.zh: 你报道军队中的脑损伤已经很久了。

sentences.en: And it seems like the scope of your reporting, it just keeps on widening.
sentences.zh: 而且看起来你的报道范围一直在扩大。

sentences.en: It keeps getting broader.
sentences.zh: 它变得越来越广。

sentences.en: And I do find that pretty concerning.
sentences.zh: 我确实觉得这很令人担忧。

sentences.en: And I wonder how your understanding of brain injuries has now shifted.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你对脑损伤的理解现在发生了怎样的转变。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I first got into this because of huge weapons that were hurting people.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是说，我最初接触这个是因为巨大的武器正在伤害人们。

sentences.en: But the more I learned, the more I realized you don't have to be around a big blast or even a small blast to get injured.
sentences.zh: 但我了解得越多，就越意识到你不需要在巨大的爆炸甚至小爆炸附近也会受伤。

sentences.en: You don't even have to hit your head.
sentences.zh: 你甚至不需要撞到头。

sentences.en: I mean, think about the surf men who are out there in the waves.
sentences.zh: 想想那些在海浪中的冲浪救援队员。

sentences.en: Their head's not coming in contact with anything, and yet they end up with a profound injury.
sentences.zh: 他们的头没有接触到任何东西，然而他们最终却受到了严重的伤害。

sentences.en: And I've really come to appreciate just how amazingly complex and delicate the brain is.
sentences.zh: 我真的开始意识到大脑是多么复杂和脆弱。

sentences.en: I mean, we're talking about an organ with 100 billion connections, which we barely understand at all.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们谈论的是一个拥有1000亿个连接的器官，而我们对此几乎一无所知。

sentences.en: And I've started to wonder what other everyday things have this kind of impact and are changing our brains.
sentences.zh: 我开始怀疑还有哪些日常事物有这种影响，正在改变我们的大脑。

sentences.en: So I think we really need to go forward with our eyes open and keep asking.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们真的需要睁大眼睛继续前进，并不断追问。

sentences.en: You know, how is modern life affecting a brain that really hasn't changed since the time we lived in caves?
sentences.zh: 你知道，现代生活是如何影响一个自我们住在洞穴时代以来就从未改变过的大脑的？

sentences.en: Well, thank you so much for your reporting, Dave.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢你的报道，戴夫。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: What are the big takeaways for you going through this process?
sentences.zh: 在经历这个过程后，你最大的收获是什么？

sentences.en: I guess I was shocked that so many people responded.
sentences.zh: 我想我感到震惊的是，竟然有这么多人回应。

sentences.en: I was just glad that people were willing to.
sentences.zh: 我只是很高兴大家愿意这样做。

sentences.en: Because, I mean, it was hard because you're reading about this and it's bringing up stuff.
sentences.zh: 因为，我是说，这很难，因为你在阅读这些内容时，会勾起一些往事。

sentences.en: And you're like, oh, wow, that makes so much sense.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得，哦，哇，原来是这样，这就说得通了。

sentences.en: And for the longest time, I was just annoyed at my dad for, like, being mad all the time.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里，我一直对我父亲总是发火感到很恼火。

sentences.en: But he was really just struggling.
sentences.zh: 但其实他当时真的在苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: It kind of maybe reframes how you understand everything that happened.
sentences.zh: 这或许能让你重新审视对过去所发生一切的理解。

sentences.en: It's really helpful to understand, like, get an image of what he was really going through inside and that he wouldn't know to tell us.
sentences.zh: 能真正理解并想象出他内心深处到底经历了什么，而他自己却不知道该如何告诉我们，这真的很有帮助。

sentences.en: He didn't know.
sentences.zh: 他自己也不知道。

sentences.en: Yeah, he didn't know.
sentences.zh: 是的，他不知道。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Monday, a divided Supreme Court allowed construction on President Trump's luxury White House ballroom to continue.
sentences.zh: 周一，最高法院以分歧意见裁定，允许继续建造特朗普总统的白宫豪华宴会厅。

sentences.en: The decision marked a significant win for Trump, who has made completing the $400 million ballroom a major priority.
sentences.zh: 这一裁决对特朗普来说是一次重大胜利，他已将完成这个耗资 4 亿美元的宴会厅列为首要任务。

sentences.en: In a 5-4 ruling, the court's majority found that the preservationists who challenged the ballroom construction did not have the legal grounds to bring their lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 在 5 比 4 的投票中，法院多数派认为，挑战宴会厅建设的保护主义者没有提起诉讼的法律依据。

sentences.en: Chief Justice John Roberts joined the court's three liberal justices in dissenting the ruling, with Roberts writing that the construction was, quote, likely unlawful.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官约翰·罗伯茨与法院的三位自由派大法官一同持反对意见，罗伯茨写道，该建筑工程“很可能是不合法的”。

sentences.en: And the Army Secretary Dan Driscoll submitted his resignation to President Trump following months of building tension with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over promotions of service members.
sentences.zh: 此外，陆军部长丹·德里斯科尔在与国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯因军人晋升问题发生数月紧张对峙后，向特朗普总统递交了辞呈。

sentences.en: Last fall, Hegseth ordered Driscoll to remove two Black and two female officers from the Army's promotion lists.
sentences.zh: 去年秋天，赫格塞斯命令德里斯科尔将两名黑人和两名女性军官从陆军晋升名单中除名。

sentences.en: Driscoll, citing their record of exemplary service, repeatedly refused, prompting a months-long standoff.
sentences.zh: 德里斯科尔以他们表现优异为由多次拒绝，引发了长达数月的僵局。

sentences.en: The Times has reported that Driscoll is now barely on speaking terms with Hegseth.
sentences.zh: 据《泰晤士报》报道，德里斯科尔现在几乎与赫格塞斯断绝了往来。

sentences.en: Hegseth has fired or forced out roughly a half-dozen senior officers, prompting questions over a widening vacuum of leadership.
sentences.zh: 赫格塞斯已经解雇或逼走了大约六名高级军官，引发了人们对领导层真空扩大的担忧。

sentences.en: Finally, a jury in Las Vegas on Monday found a man guilty of orchestrating the 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur,
sentences.zh: 最后，拉斯维加斯的一个陪审团周一裁定一名男子策划了 1996 年图派克·沙库尔的谋杀案，

sentences.en: delivering a conviction nearly 30 years after one of the most notorious killings in hip-hop.
sentences.zh: 在嘻哈音乐界最臭名昭著的谋杀案发生近 30 年后，终于做出了有罪判决。

sentences.en: Dwayne Keith Davis was accused of obtaining the gun used in the shooting and pursuing Shakur during a gang war
sentences.zh: 德韦恩·基思·戴维斯被指控在帮派战争中获取了枪击案中使用的枪支并追杀沙库尔，

sentences.en: that became entangled in the feud between East Coast and West Coast hip-hop labels.
sentences.zh: 这场帮派战争卷入了东西海岸嘻哈厂牌之间的纷争。

sentences.en: Davis was found guilty of first-degree murder.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯被判一级谋杀罪成立。

sentences.en: He promised he would appeal.
sentences.zh: 他承诺会提出上诉。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是睡到不省人事。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
